name: Traditionalism
summary: Traditionalism, in the sense of the Perennialist school founded by René Guénon, holds that a single primordial metaphysical truth underlies all orthodox religions and that the modern world is a deviation from it, marked by rationalism, materialism, individualism, equality and belief in progress. Politically it favours a hierarchy of natural functions or castes, authority descending from a spiritual source and not from the people, and rejects democracy and egalitarianism. Guénon himself regarded the social sphere as secondary and stayed aloof from party politics, while Julius Evola drew a more activist, aristocratic and warrior-centred politics from the same premises.
scope: The Traditionalist or Perennialist school as documented in Wikipedia's Traditionalism (perennialism): Guénon (chiefly The Crisis of the Modern World), with Schuon, Coomaraswamy and Nasr on religion and modernity, and Evola for the political and social implications (Men Among the Ruins, Ride the Tiger, Pagan Imperialism, read through Furlong's scholarship). The catalog name 'Traditionalism' points at a disambiguation page, so this profile excludes the other senses audited separately or not at all: Spanish Traditionalism (traditionalism-2), Burkean traditionalist conservatism, Carlism, and Traditionalist Catholicism. Where Guénon and Evola differ (priestly versus warrior primacy, quietism versus activism), the answer follows Guénon unless stated; many political questions are inferred and marked low.

sources.title: The Crisis of the Modern World

sources.usedFor: Caste as individual nature, equality as pseudo-principle, the argument against democracy, power from above, industry and materialism, individualism, the 'armed nation' and the Kali-Yuga.

sources.title: Traditionalism (perennialism)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Core doctrines (primordial tradition, transcendent unity of religions, Schuon's list of modernity's traits), Nasr on ecology and growth, and political reception.

sources.usedFor: Evola on the traditional state, hierarchy, rights, equality, nationalism versus empire, race, and totalitarianism.

sources.author: Wikiquote, compiling Julius Evola
sources.usedFor: Evola on democracy, sacral kingship, hierarchy, women and the family, war, consumer civilization and education.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Guénon treats social and economic arrangements as downstream of principle, so the school has no stated line on health systems; adherents split between organic duty and anti-statism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage doctrine in the sources; Guénon criticises economic factors dominating life but does not address wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Guénon blames the dominance of industry, commerce and finance on the modern materialist outlook, so a claim that markets are the best allocator would not be endorsed; inferred, not stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Neither nationalisation nor private ownership of utilities is discussed; the school regards the economic sphere as secondary to the spiritual and hierarchical order.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Guénon notes that wealth has become the only surviving social distinction but proposes no fiscal remedy; adherents are split or indifferent.

unions-good.rationale: Modern class-based unions are not addressed; Guénon admires pre-modern craftsmen but treats class organisation as part of the egalitarian mentality.

property-fundamental.rationale: Evola separates aristocracy from plutocracy and puts rank above wealth, but the sources state no doctrine of property rights; split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Guénon sees finance steering politics yet offers no regulatory programme, so the answer is inferred as indifference.

cut-welfare.rationale: No stated view; the ideal of the privileged looking after the dependent sits against Evola's rejection of citizens' rights, so adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Guénon criticises workers reduced to machine-slaves but nowhere endorses collective ownership; an egalitarian economic scheme runs against caste hierarchy (inferred).

surveillance-ok.rationale: Evola's state is an authoritative source of order and not a guarantor of citizens' rights, but surveillance is not discussed; split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Evola's contempt for the modern 'animal ideal' of comfort and from the school's moral conservatism; no source speaks to drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Guénon says modern ideas such as equality are the only things not open to discussion, which is a complaint about enforced orthodoxy; inferred opposition to speech codes.

strong-leader.rationale: Furlong's account has Evola treating absolutist and totalitarian rule as a degradation of the traditional state, in which authority rests on natural hierarchical recognition rather than a leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Evola treats the state as the source of authority and sovereignty for the differentiated man, and Guénon requires power from above, so the anarchist claim is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; split between order-minded and anti-state instincts.

empower-police-military.rationale: Evola praises martial order and Prussian state structure, but Guénon opposes mass militarism; no statement on funding, so split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the school's sacralised view of sexuality and Evola's anti-hedonist stance; not stated for this question.

decide-locally.rationale: The traditional order is hierarchical and organic, with a supranational imperial apex in Evola; localism versus centralism is not the axis, so split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical, authority-based view of justice that stresses order over treatment; Guénon does not address penology.

traditional-family.rationale: Guénon cites the Hindu prophecy of an age when castes mingle and the family no longer exists as a mark of the present crisis, and Evola makes the father's spiritual authority the family anchor.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Redefining the family would be read as part of the dissolution Guénon laments and conflicts with Evola's authority-centred family; inferred from those principles.

abortion-legal.rationale: The school regards human life as grounded in a transcendent order and modernity as a descent from it; abortion is not discussed directly, so this is inferred from that principle and the family stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: Guénon argues that true power can be legitimised only by a spiritual authority standing above the social order, which makes religion central to public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Egalitarian remedial programmes conflict with Evola's hierarchical race doctrine and Guénon's rejection of equality; neither addresses the policy itself.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Evola holds that women and men differ in nature and that feminism shows men losing virility, so gender is a given of nature and Tradition.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Guénon wants to preserve traditional civilizations against modern levelling, though he and Evola ground this in traditional forms or empire rather than the nation as such.

gradual-change.rationale: Guénon holds that no reconstitution can start from the social level and warns against rebuilding from consequences, which favours slow work from principles; the quiz item is only loosely matched.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in these sources; adherents split between cultural-preservation and universalist leanings.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Evola's supranational ideal is a hierarchical empire, not egalitarian bodies like the UN; Guénon dismisses modern humanitarian internationalism as unserious.

free-trade.rationale: Guénon decries trade competition as the dominant influence between peoples; no endorsement of free trade, inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Furlong reports Evola viewing nationalism as the offspring of liberalism and bourgeois modernity, and Guénon traces modern nations to the destruction of feudalism and medieval Christendom.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Guénon calls the fashionable humanitarianism not worth taking seriously, so rights-based intervention is not a Traditionalist cause; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Not stated; follows from the emphasis on distinct traditional civilizations, though the school is not nativist in the usual way.

limit-growth.rationale: Nasr criticises measuring society by economic growth and links the ecological crisis to a broken harmony with the sacred, which supports limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Nasr sees the environmental crisis as spiritual in origin and criticises scientism, but he proposes no state programme, so a call for drastic government action is a split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Guénon argues that modern industry has made men slaves of machines and calls 'progress' a lay dogma, so faith in technological salvation is the opposite of his position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the critique of industrial technology as spiritually and ecologically damaging; not discussed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Guénon names the Revolution as a result of usurpation and 'subversion' is Evola's word for modern change, though Evola grants the differentiated man the right to oppose a decadent state.

experts-over-public.rationale: Guénon argues real competence belongs to a minority and is excluded by majority rule, though he doubts specialist expertise in modern form.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from Guénon's dislike of uniformity and of the economy dominating life; not discussed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not stated; the premise that economic arrangements are central is itself foreign to a school that ranks them below spiritual principles.

land-value-tax.rationale: An economic technicality outside the sources; indifferent.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Evola defends aristocracy and hereditary rank, so heavy inheritance levies cut against it; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Guénon puts economic arrangements below spiritual principle and the sources give no view on income schemes; unconditional payments are neither endorsed nor condemned.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Guénon criticises industry and trade competition alike, and the policy is not addressed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred: promoting industrial development is what Guénon blames the modern world for pursuing.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Guénon praises pre-modern craftsmen yet states no property doctrine; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Guénon takes the Marxist abolition of classes to be the negation of natural hierarchy; inferred rather than stated about wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon only notes that politics seems controlled by finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Furlong reports Evola placing the corporation among the lower levels of the hierarchical state, which fits state-recognised bodies; the specific wage-setting scheme is not stated.

one-party-rule.rationale: Evola criticised totalitarian bureaucratic regimes as a degradation of the traditional state, and Guénon dismisses party politics as mere outward signs.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Evola laments that true sovereigns with divine-right authority have vanished and holds that surviving monarchies lack real power; Guénon treats the royal function as legitimate but subordinate to spiritual authority.

democracy-best.rationale: Guénon calls the democratic idea a sophism, arguing the higher cannot proceed from the lower and that majority rule is the law of matter and brute force.

direct-votes.rationale: Guénon says the opinion of the majority is an expression of incompetence and universal suffrage an illusion; direct legislation by the masses would deepen this. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

workers-councils.rationale: Power from below and class rule run against Guénon's principle that authority comes from above; inferred from his critique of democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Evola prefers a supranational empire but no source speaks to secession; split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Guénon defines caste as individual nature predisposing each man to a function and blames the denial of these differences for the social chaos.

political-violence-never.rationale: Evola gives war and combat a spiritual value and says danger reawakens the spirit, so he would not hold violence never justified; Guénon is quietist but does not renounce force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Evola's Metaphysics of War attributes anti-materialist, spiritual value to war and heroism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Guénon states that the temporal power's independence from spiritual authority is the first usurpation opening the way to modern disorder.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Guénon views traditional civilizations as ordered by principles descending from revelation, with law legitimised by spiritual authority, though he gives no programme for scripture-based statutes.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Evola's state is the source of sovereignty and authority, so privatising courts and defence is incompatible; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Evola values martial ethos but sees nations as tools, not ends; Guénon does not address; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Furlong reports Evola rejecting blood-based nationalism for a spiritual-race and imperial model, and Evola calls blood-and-soil a regression to totemism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Guénon names 'historical materialism' as a modern suggestion and denies that economic factors drive history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Guénon says equality can exist nowhere because no two beings are alike, and calls the egalitarian idea fantastical.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Traditionalists value surviving traditional peoples but the sources do not discuss land authority; split.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from Guénon's rejection of egalitarian moralism and Evola's contempt for non-European peoples; not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Evola favours a supranational imperial order over nations, and Guénon envisages East-West intellectual understanding; the statement's religion/civilization link is only loosely matched.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Guénon condemns individualism as the negation of any principle above the individual and attacks the pursuit of material ends.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Furlong reports that Evola finds no place for individual rights or the Rights of Man, only differentiated duties and rights according to station.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nasr calls for restoring a sense of the sacred toward nature and criticises seeing nature as a mere resource.

limit-population.rationale: Nasr's ecological critique could support restraint, but the school's family-centred ethic cuts against state limits; no stated position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Guénon calls the modern world a material, quantitative civilization whose people have become slaves of machines, and treats it as a crisis and deviation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Guénon sees technological development as the main aim of the modern world and as a servitude, so accelerating it despite institutional disruption is opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Schuon's and Nasr's rejection of scientism and materialism; not directly discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: handing judgement to machines compounds the reduction of intelligence to a 'tool for making tools' that Guénon criticises.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Technology policy on privacy lies outside the school's texts; adherents split between anti-surveillance and pro-authority instincts.

restore-past-order.rationale: Guénon seeks restoration of traditional intellectuality and civilization, holding modernity an anomaly and deviation from the normal order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Guénon says indifference to truth begets pragmatism, and he holds politics should follow principles, not results.

direct-action.rationale: Guénon holds social action is derivative and cannot start reconstitution; Evola's later stance is not clearly activist; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Guénon says reconstruction must start from principles, which suggests means matter, but Evola's warrior ethos does not tie methods to the end state; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Traditional civilizations in Guénon's account are settled, hierarchical and priestly, not primitive; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guénon decries factory specialisation but grounds social function in caste, a form of division of functions by nature.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from rejection of egalitarian uniformity; not stated.

production-for-use.rationale: Guénon criticises quantity over quality yet states no economic arrangement; split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The school rejects the Marxist reading of society as class conflict, though it also condemns the dominance of finance; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by the lowest social level inverts the hierarchy Guénon defends, since the higher cannot proceed from the lower.

collective-farming.rationale: Not stated; collectivisation is inferred to conflict with organic, hierarchical order.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Guénon sees trade competition as a modern determinant of relations between peoples but calls economic causes means rather than ultimate causes; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Evola's state is a source of authority above the individual, so a libertarian view of tax is rejected; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Guénon denies that individuals are the measure of social order, and Furlong has Evola rejecting individual rights; the harm principle presumes them.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Furlong reports Evola rejecting individual rights for differentiated rights by condition, and Guénon calls the individualism that underlies them a negation of principle.

conscription.rationale: Guénon condemns the 'armed nation' and general mobilisation as products of egalitarian, quantitative modernity.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Guénon rejects voting as a source of authority yet the sources say nothing about a right to leave; no position.

state-as-business.rationale: Guénon condemns the domination of finance and commerce over politics; running the state as a business reverses the proper order.

positive-liberty.rationale: Evola speaks of differentiated liberty, the freedom to be what one is, but gives no material-means doctrine; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Guénon does claim that suggestion and opinion-making steer politics, but names no particular institutions; split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Evola ranked races through a doctrine of body, soul and spirit and endorsed hierarchy, but the Guénonian mainstream does not take a genetic view; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Furlong reports Evola placing family and corporation in an organic hierarchy, and Guénon holds that representation by majority counts is invalid.

total-state.rationale: Evola faults totalitarianism for its centralised bureaucracy as a degradation of the traditional state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Evola's 'revolt' envisions renewal through a spiritual aristocracy, but he is pessimistic about reversal and Guénon rejects nationalist projects; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Evola favours a spiritual, not materialist, imperialism and calls nationalist conquest chauvinism; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Evola's traditional state rests on loyalty and sovereignty, which resembles feudal oaths, but the exact claim is not stated.

bound-labor.rationale: Hierarchical estates are accepted but legal serfdom is not discussed; split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Guénon rejects relativism and holds that real knowledge is intellectual and derives from principle, not power; he also treats modern ideas as 'suggestions' pushed by interest, which is not the same claim.

universal-morality.rationale: The school holds a single primordial metaphysical truth beneath all orthodox religions, though it is reached by intellection rather than ordinary reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Guénon defines the community by a principle above individuals and rejects treating it as a sum of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Evola's views on Jews are given by Furlong as spirit-based, but a Jewish state is not a Traditionalist topic; split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Evola subordinates nation and homeland to an imperial order, so a right of return based on descent is not a school concern.

revive-national-language.rationale: Guénon values traditional languages and forms as vehicles of doctrine, but state-led revival of a national tongue is a nationalist project the sources do not address.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rule by numbers in the workplace reproduces what Guénon calls the democratic error of majority competence.

school-vouchers.rationale: Guénon criticises compulsory uniform education but states no voucher policy; split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Technical economic policy outside the sources; indifferent.

economic-freedom.rationale: The school ranks economic factors below spiritual ones, so an economic precondition for political freedom is rejected; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Evola's aristocracy of spirit leads by embodied quality, but reliance on moral example in place of law is not stated.

national-self-determination.rationale: Evola treats the nation as subordinate to empire, whereas Guénon says nations arose from the destruction of medieval unity; the principle itself is not endorsed or condemned.

force-without-un.rationale: Evola's imperial order does not rest on international bodies, but the sources do not discuss the legality of force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Schuon lists rationalism among modernity's defining errors, and the school holds knowledge comes through intellection within an orthodox tradition, so reason alone as guide is rejected.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Evola builds rank on spirit rather than citizenship and the sources do not discuss welfare eligibility; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Evola's ethos of duty and discipline could favour work requirements, but welfare conditionality is not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Guénon sees castes as functions fitted to each man's nature, which implies cooperation among functions, not struggle between classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The school defends inherited tradition and condemns the modern break with the past.

dominated-front.rationale: Guénon defends the East's independence against Western domination but proposes no political bloc; split.

workers-nation.rationale: Evola derides both class internationalism and the nation as a supreme entity; the working class as a political agent has no place.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Evola holds women and men are not comparable, with the father as spiritual head of the family, supporting distinct public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Evola distinguishes merchant values from higher ones, but the sources give no stance on usury law; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Evola's spiritual racism is hierarchical but he rejected crude biological racism; legal segregation is not stated for the school.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The school treats the state as the bearer of authority from above, not a tool of an economic class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from Nasr's critique of industrial exploitation of nature; not discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Guénon defends traditional civilizations and distinction among peoples but not forced assimilation; the sources do not address migration.

elite-replacement.rationale: Guénon alleges directed suggestion by those with an interest in confusion, but not replacement of a native population; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The school rejects counting heads as a basis of authority; the electoral formula is not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Evola sees nations as tools and rejects nationalist chauvinism; a mission to export regimes is not endorsed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Evola affirms male superiority as natural and hierarchical, so he would deny that this is an injustice, though the sources do not address the claim as framed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Guénon says politicians' incompetence is mirrored in majority opinion and that real control lies behind the scenes; the claim is not made in populist terms.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not a Traditionalist doctrine and Evola prioritised spiritual over bodily race; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Evola's state commands from authority and not under citizen rights, but the sources do not discuss past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The school's state is a source of authority, hierarchy and spiritual order, not a minimal protector of property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Evola's racial writings address spiritual race and hierarchy; the sources do not give a settled school position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Guénon calls equality a pseudo-principle and negation of hierarchy, and Furlong reports Evola allowing no equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate foreign to the school; no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Guénon criticises Western domination by material force, but the labelling of settler states is not in the sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the school's preference for differentiated law according to status and tradition.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Traditionalists hold orthodox religions equally valid paths and advise staying within one's tradition, but the law is not discussed; split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; Hindu cultural sentiment is respected, but the policy is not addressed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Guénon criticises uniform secular, bookish compulsory education and wants knowledge tied to principles.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist question outside the school; no position.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Guénon says the people cannot confer a power they lack and that true power can only come from above, legitimised by spiritual authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon dislikes trade-competition as a determinant but states nothing on balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Evola's spiritual-race and imperial framing does not call for expelling minorities, and Furlong notes his criticism of biological nationalism; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Evola values the warrior ethos and heroism and defends imperial order, which rules out an absolute non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Guénon rejects the idea of progress and the cult of competition and quantity as modern suggestions.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Guénon sees parties as outward signs of modern confusion, but the sources do not discuss banning them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon accepts domination by right of hierarchy, so split.

separated-powers.rationale: Guénon requires spiritual authority above temporal power, not checks among equals; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: A revolutionary vanguard of the working class is foreign to a school that places authority in a spiritual elite; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Evola's noblesse oblige suggests duty toward the dependent, but he ranks by spirit and not by need; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is outside the sources; neither wide ownership nor public housing is a Traditionalist concern.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Guénon counts class conflict as a product of the denial of caste and function, which favours restraint on strikes; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Guénon traces social disorder to the loss of principles and hierarchy and not to numbers; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Guénon says distinction among peoples does not mean opposition, and Evola sees cohesion in hierarchy not ethnicity; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Guénon requires offices to fall to those whose nature fits the function, which a lottery would contradict.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Evola's state is not bound by citizens' rights but he criticised terror-based absolutism; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic emergency measures are not addressed by the school; indifferent.

party-controls-media.rationale: Evola opposed totalitarian regimes; media control by a party is inferred to be rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Evola treated party-based totalitarianism as a degraded state; the Prussian model is praised instead.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed; the school's categories are spiritual rank and tradition, not nationality.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Guénon wants rulers selected for competence and rank, not tied to average status; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Guénon dismisses party politics as only outward signs; no position on discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Evola's supranational ideal is a hierarchical spiritual empire, not a bureaucratic union; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Evola praised a sovereign-centred, aristocratic and military Prussian-style state, supporting executive command by the head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Guénon defends the Catholic Church's hierarchical form against Protestant individualism, and the school favours hierarchical authority in religion.

clerical-rule.rationale: Guénon places the sacerdotal power above the royal, though Evola favours kings and warriors over priests.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Evola rejects internationalism and class politics, and the school offers no support for wartime defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Evola criticises debasing mass culture and compulsory schooling, but he does not state a censorship doctrine.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Evola favours lasting sovereignty over elected terms but does not discuss presidential term rules.

recall-officials.rationale: Guénon denies that power flows from below, so recall by electors reverses the order.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Evola envisions an imperial order, not isolation; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed; mandated universal ownership is inferred to be a modern egalitarian scheme.

people-in-arms.rationale: Guénon calls the 'armed nation' and mass uprising a product of egalitarianism and numbers.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nasr's criticisms of modern urban industrial life and nostalgia for traditional civilization suggest agreement; not stated as such.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nation as such is not a Traditionalist end; split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Guénon's complaint is against education that puts memory in the place of intelligence, not against the educated as a class.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Guénon ranks traditional civilizations above the modern West, which he calls a deviation, so not all civilizations are equally valid.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the authority-based, order-first conception of the state; not discussed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from rejection of gender egalitarianism; not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Guénon attacks evolutionism as a modern error but does not defend literal creationism in schools; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Evola condemns the modern 'animal ideal' of comfort and pleasure; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Evola sees blood as inferior to spirit, but the school gives no citizenship rule; split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Guénon values traditional civilizations and their forms in general, but language policy is not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Traditionalism favours the protection of orthodox religious forms, though exemption law is not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Guénon condemns individualism as the denial of anything above the individual and values conformity to tradition.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Guénon sees finance as a leading power over modern politics but gives no view on cancelling debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed; economic transformation is not central.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A constitution made by the vote of the people is an instance of power from below which Guénon rejects.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The school ranks economic growth below spiritual ends, so sacrificing freedoms for it is unlikely; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon doubts humanitarianism but praises traditional duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Evola values martial strength, but the sources do not discuss weapons policy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state chosen by popular vote is power from below; the school prefers legitimation from above.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Guénon sees finance as controlling politics but does not discuss central banking.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Evola treats the fatherland as a tool and not an end, so a claim to historic land is not a school principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Evola places the individual and corporation below the hierarchy of the state, which fits subordination of property; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Guénon opposes Marxism wholesale as materialism and does not enter debates among its critics.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Nasr's ecological stance is sympathetic, but the principle is not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: Evola's imperial vision implies binding links among states but treaty doctrine is not in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Evola holds nations to be tools of empire and not rights-holders, and the school has no doctrine on annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Guénon names the temporal power's subordination of spiritual authority as the initial usurpation that opens the way to all others.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Guénon sees party politics as only outward signs of modern confusion, and a sovereign above parties fits a legitimation from above.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Evola favours an imperial hierarchy that holds nations together, but secession is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy within an empire fits Evola's picture of nations ordered under a higher unit, but no source states this about regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Evola laments the disappearance of sovereigns with divine-right authority, and sacral kingship belongs to Traditionalist political thought.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the school's concerns.

character-from-environment.rationale: Guénon defines caste as individual nature, with aptitudes that predispose a man to a function, so character is innate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Evola holds that absolutism is a degradation of the traditional state, where authority rests on natural hierarchical recognition and spiritual sanction, not arbitrary will.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from Guénon's criticism of technical development as the goal of the modern world.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not discussed; hierarchy is the principle, not mixture.

leader-cult.rationale: Evola criticised the Volk-based populism of Nazism and the cult of the nation as a mystical entity.

equal-parenting.rationale: Evola ties family authority to the father, which cuts against an equal-time presumption, but the legal question is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Guénon rejects class struggle as a driver of history and does not discuss it within socialist states.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not discussed; confiscation for the cultivators is an egalitarian scheme, inferred to be rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: Not a question the school addresses; its categories are spiritual rank and tradition.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Evola rejects blood-and-soil nationalism as a regression to totemism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Traditionalists treat belonging to an orthodox religion as the necessary path, but legal punishment is not addressed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Nasr's Islamic traditionalism upholds dress codes, but Guénon and Evola do not address legislation; split.

common-currency.rationale: Guénon sees finance as dominating modern life but gives no view on monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Evola's unity is spiritual and imperial, not by ancestry or language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Evola places nations beneath empire, which could accommodate minority self-government, but this is not stated.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Evola rejects rights-based politics, and Zionism or emigration is not addressed by the school.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Guénon rejects 'historical materialism' as a modern suggestion and says economic factors are means, not causes.

ban-cartels.rationale: Guénon criticises the dominance of commerce and finance but proposes no competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed; Guénon's criticism of finance suggests no sympathy for banks, but also none for market purism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Guénon thinks majority opinion is an expression of incompetence, so it should not rule courts or institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Evola holds the sexes are not interchangeable and denies equality, so quotas run against it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Guénon criticises industrial trade competition and Western economic expansion, which hints at sympathy for autarky, but no bloc doctrine is stated.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not discussed; Nasr's ecological concerns are sympathetic.

moral-incentives.rationale: Guénon criticises the primacy of material interests and money-making; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Evola's later work counsels immunity to decadence more than programme, and he does not endorse revolutionary vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Guénon treats hierarchy of caste, and Evola of aristocracy, as natural principles of order, and both oppose levelling.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Guénon wants Westerners to recover their own traditional civilization, but the statement's nation-centred framing is only loosely matched.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Guénon rejects the West's claim to superiority and dismisses its civilizing mission, though he accepts rank within a tradition.

patriotic-education.rationale: Evola regards patriotism as subordinate to the order of empire; split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon rejects equality as principle but states nothing on preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary questions are not discussed; Guénon's remarks on finance's power are not a policy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Guénon discusses the modern world's crisis in cyclical terms and not capitalism's economic crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Evola favours imperial order in a spiritual sense; not discussed in these terms.

delink-world-market.rationale: Guénon wants the East left independent of Western material domination, which favours delinking, but he states no economic programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist category outside the school's analysis of caste and nature.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Evola accepts differentiated rights by station and denies equal rights, so a legal duty not to discriminate would be foreign; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Furlong reports Evola rejecting the Rights of Man and individual rights in favour of differentiated ones.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Guénon condemns Western domination by force but the sources do not discuss treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Guénon says power comes from above and the people cannot confer it; election by the political nation reverses this.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; the principle of hierarchical authority implies the superior decides.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Evola grants the differentiated man the right to oppose a decadent state, but Guénon is quietist; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Guénon criticises parliamentary majorities as incompetence and says power flows from above.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; traditional religions differ.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Nasr's call for harmony with nature and sacred sense implies humane use; not stated.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Evola distinguishes aristocracy from plutocracy and ties rank to duty and quality.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Guénon says the social domain is not where reconstitution can start and keeps clear of party quarrels, but Evola urges action; split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Evola criticises mass culture and the consumer civilization as leveling; Guénon calls modern ideas suggestions that manufacture opinion.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Guénon says opinion is manufactured by suggestion, which resembles this, but he frames it as directed by interested parties rather than an economic class; split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Guénon condemns Western material power over the East but offers a spiritual and not an economic explanation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Evola bases rank on spirit and not on birthplace; office-holding rules are not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate within communism; the school stands outside it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Guénon favours the East's independence from the West but states no development doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Evola treats nations as tools of empire; split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Evola's hierarchy is by spirit and not descent from first peoples; not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Furlong shows Evola as a radical-right influence, and the school rejects the democratic constitutional consensus; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Evola rejected totalitarianism as degraded, but also admired aspects of fascism; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute outside the sources; adherents are likely split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The school defends inherited tradition against modern iconoclasm; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Evola blames men's loss of virility for feminism but does not address policy; split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Evola's views on the sexes address nature and authority and not service provision.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Guénon argues that Western modern institutions are a deviation from traditional civilization and that every traditional civilization has its own forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Evola praised Prussia's state-centered, aristocratic and military structure; a political guardian role is inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the school's view of traditional gender roles; not discussed.

filial-duty.rationale: Guénon lists the end of the family as a mark of the dark age, and traditional hierarchy includes the respect due to elders and fathers.

office-by-exam.rationale: Guénon criticises bookish learning that puts memory in place of intelligence; selection by examination is therefore doubtful, split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Guénon criticises the dominance of finance but gives no view on investment screening.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Guénon sees the dissolution of the family as a marker of the crisis; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Guénon denies that power derives from below, so binding mandates reverse the order.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure is not discussed; the school's own ideal is hierarchical estates, not use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Guénon dismisses parliaments but the sources do not discuss budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed; Guénon values traditional forms over state uniformity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; foreigners' property is outside the school's concerns.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The notion that unequal outcomes imply injustice rests on the equality that Guénon calls a fantastical pseudo-principle.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Evola criticises the 'animal ideal' of comfort and a consumer civilization, and Guénon calls modern civilization quantitative and material.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Evola's warrior ethos does not decide the question of covert war and the sources do not discuss it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Evola's imperial hierarchy suggests a lead power, but intervention to hold allies is not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Guénon says politics seems controlled by finance and commerce, which suggests agreement that business holds undue influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Guénon alleges directed suggestion of public opinion, but foreign funding rules are not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from family-centred traditionalism; not directly documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; the school has no doctrine of local land rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: Guénon criticises people placed in functions unfit for their nature, which cuts against a general job guarantee, but the policy is not discussed.

democratic-peace.rationale: Guénon denies that democracy is a legitimate order and attacks pacifism and humanitarianism as dreams of modernist progress.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Furlong notes the traditional state's command and obedience rest on natural hierarchical recognition.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon opposes Western domination of the East, but a general rule is not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed; Guénon admires craft over modern industry, but craft unions are not mentioned.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Evola's antisemitism concerned a spirit of subversion and wrote on the Protocols; typical adherents of the mainstream do not hold the claim as school doctrine, so split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The family is a core traditional institution for the school; abolishing legal marriage is its dissolution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Evola's authoritative state is not built on citizens' rights; transparency is not discussed.

local-production.rationale: Guénon favours the craftsman's qualitative production against mass quantity; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The school favours hierarchical orders and initiatory organisations rather than anarchist affinity groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Evola sees nations as subordinate to empire, which cuts both ways.

religious-nation.rationale: Evola places nations below an imperial spiritual order; the sources give no clear position.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Evola's imperial order has hierarchy among peoples, but tributary diplomacy is not discussed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism lies outside the school's concerns.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Guénon sets no doctrine for personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Guénon regards Marxist historical materialism as an extreme form of the modern materialism he opposes.

religion-illusion.rationale: Traditionalism holds that religion transmits a transcendent truth, and Schuon counts atheism and materialism among modernity's errors.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Guénon rejects the idea of progress and the cult of material production as modern deviation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The school denies sexual equality in the first place, and gives priority to spiritual over economic causes.

socialized-care.rationale: Guénon sees the dissolution of the family as a mark of crisis, so transferring its functions to the state opposes it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon's interest is in doctrinal and sacred languages.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not discussed; not within the school's concerns.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A voluntarist egalitarian community scheme is not part of the school's hierarchical order; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Evola rejects ethnic nationalism, but the policy of settling majorities is not discussed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Guénon criticises materialism in both its liberal commercial and Marxist forms, and Evola's tradition is explicitly neither bourgeois nor communist.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Evola treats the fatherland as a tool and not as an end, so land claims by tie of history are not a school principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Furlong says Evola's failure to condemn the Holocaust was a mistake; Evola did not deny it outright in this account, and denial is not school doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Guénon and Evola do not address it; adherents split between moral disapproval and anti-state restraint.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Evola faulted terror-based absolutism, though he is not a liberal about opposition; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Guénon holds that spiritual authority legitimises temporal power, so protection of religion by law fits; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Guénon condemns Western domination of the East by brute force and material power.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Guénon notes that the East seeks independence, not conquest, but does not state a jihad doctrine; split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Guénon says power without spiritual sanction is counterfeit, but he is quietist about overthrow; split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Guénon argues that rule by the people is a contradiction in terms and that majority opinion expresses incompetence.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Evola denies sexual and racial equality and the premise of oppression, and Guénon rejects equality; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The school treats sex roles as grounded in nature and Tradition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the view of life as grounded in a transcendent order; not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Guénon holds political categories to be outward signs and himself above party quarrels, but also rejects blending modern ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Guénon says modern workers have become slaves of machines, unlike former craftsmen, for whom intelligent work was possible.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Guénon and Schuon became Muslim and the school works with Islamic traditionalism, so a clash of civilizations thesis is not its position.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Guénon says true power can only come from above and is legitimised by the sanction of spiritual authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Traditionalists favour visible religious forms, so banning them would be opposed; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic regime is secondary for Guénon; neither laissez-faire nor state planning is endorsed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Evola gives warrior values high spiritual rank, and Guénon mocks the pacifist dream of ending all war.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is not discussed; Guénon's dislike of industrial progress cuts against it, but no doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Guénon wants the East independent of Western power, which favours neutrality, but no policy on blocs is stated.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession fits sacral kingship and aristocratic order, though Evola's emphasis is on spiritual quality; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon's critique of finance does not extend to debt policy.

property-franchise.rationale: The school rejects universal suffrage but does not discuss property qualifications; split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Evola treats sexual polarity as natural, and an ecofeminist link is foreign to the school.

reification.rationale: Guénon criticises quantity and matter ruling life, which resembles the claim, but he does not use this Marxist framing; split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Guénon says opinion is manufactured and finance steers politics, in rough agreement, though from a non-Marxist standpoint.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Furlong's Evola grounds authority in natural hierarchy and not in legal procedure; the sources do not address rule by decree versus standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Evola's hierarchy is of spirit more than blood and the sources do not support a racial franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Guénon calls the democratic idea a sophism and mass participation an influence of suggestion.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency tools are not discussed; Guénon mistrusts manufactured opinion but not for this question.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Traditionalism holds that one should stay within an orthodox tradition, but the law is not discussed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not part of school doctrine; Evola's antisemitism was cultural-spiritual in Furlong's account.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Guénon says majority opinion is incompetent, and a random citizen body is power from below.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The school insists on orthodox forms and traditional doctrine, and sees modernist adaptation as part of modern deviation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Guénon notes wealth is the only surviving social distinction but values hierarchy over liberty; split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Evola prizes a virile warrior ethos and traditional sex roles; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Schuon counts atheism among the defining errors of modernity. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Evola places authority and order at the core of the state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not discussed; the school's solution to division is hierarchy under spiritual authority.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the duties of the privileged and organic communities over a state-welfare concept of rights; not stated.

term-limits.rationale: Guénon rejects election as a source of authority and thus does not take a view on limits for elected officials.

vote-delegation.rationale: Guénon rejects rule by counting votes as the law of matter.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Nasr's ecological concern is sympathetic but extinction risk as a policy priority is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Traditionalists tie esotericism to orthodox religious forms, which are generally male-led, and Evola holds the sexes are not comparable.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Evola stresses the father's spiritual authority as the family's anchor.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Guénon rejects universal suffrage in the first place; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon treats modern production as quantitative but gives no view on patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Evola values the warrior ethos but is critical of mass regimes; split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Guénon wants the East left independent of Western domination by force, which hints at sympathy, but basing is not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Furlong notes Evola's failure to condemn the Holocaust, but the school has no doctrine on formal recognition by states.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; hierarchy by nature, not by labour or property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Evola's warrior ethos and the school's acceptance of war make absolute pacifism foreign.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Evola's genealogy is of spiritual origins and Tradition, not of nations.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The school holds that sexual difference is part of nature and Tradition.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Evola treats women as having a distinct nature, so the category is fixed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Evola gives heroism and sacrifice spiritual weight, but the cult of national martyrs is a nationalist idea; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Furlong describes Evola's 'hidden war' of history, between forces of Tradition and subversion.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Evola does not treat a homeland as the end of politics; the diaspora model is not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Guénon argues reconstitution must begin with principles and not at the social level, which gives priority to the intellectual over the state, but nation-building is not discussed; split.

god-not-male.rationale: The school affirms orthodox religious language and forms.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Traditionalism holds that tradition judges individuals, not the reverse.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Evola's antisemitism was about spirit and not economic control, per Furlong, and the school has no ethnic economic doctrine.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Evola prefers imperial order to ethnic units; not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from the state is not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Guénon denies that power comes from below, but whether a society counts as socialist is not his question.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not discussed; ownership of utilities is secondary to the school.

second-chamber.rationale: The school prefers hierarchical organisation of representation, but the second chamber is not stated; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Not discussed; the school has no economic ownership doctrine.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from hierarchical, vertical authority, which contrasts with confederal assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family model with the father as head; not stated.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed; outside the school's concerns.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the critique of scientism and attempts to overcome human limits; not stated.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed; digital finance is outside the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; digital privacy is outside the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Furlong reports that for Evola the individual, family and corporation are lower levels that conform to the state and cannot shape it.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The school's core doctrine is that human beings are rooted in a transcendent order of which modernity loses sight; Schuon names materialism as a modern error.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Evola's hierarchical state implies central authority, but regional autonomy is not discussed.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from Nasr's critique of manipulation of nature as mere resource.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from Nasr's criticism of modern industrial life; not directly discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Evola's spiritual race doctrine is not the school's mainstream; split.

racial-pride.rationale: Evola's 'race of the spirit' is not the same as racial pride; split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Evola gives war spiritual value beyond defence, and heroism justifies it.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Evola rejects blood-and-soil and ethnic nationalism for spiritual empire.

communal-electorates.rationale: Guénon rejects mass suffrage anyway, and separate electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Guénon alleges directed influence on opinion but no foreign partition plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Guénon criticises mass compulsory bookish education but gives no view on tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed; ecological concern is spiritual.

future-generations.rationale: Nasr's concern for harmony with nature implies stewardship, though the quiz framing is not his.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Evola holds that women have a distinct nature, but he would not call for giving more weight to those values in politics; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Guénon mocks the pacifist dream of ending war but states no doctrine on arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The sources contain no doctrine of diplomatic procedure; Guénon's remarks on manufactured opinion do not extend to treaty secrecy.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon's critique of finance does not reach capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Evola's state is the holder of sovereignty and command; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Evola values the warrior ethos and obedience, and Guénon's order depends on authority.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon's craft ideal is not about bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Income-support design is outside the sources and the school ranks economic arrangements below spiritual and hierarchical principles.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Budget and borrowing rules are not addressed in the sources; Guénon's criticism of finance does not become a fiscal doctrine.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Guénon wants the East free from Western domination, which suggests sympathy, but economic restructuring is not discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Evola treats the state as the source of authority and does not favour its destruction, though he would replace the modern state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Not discussed; the school has a fixed hierarchical ideal rather than an openness to experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Nasr criticises seeing nature as a resource, which is what pricing it as capital does.

sacred-nation.rationale: Furlong reports Evola seeing nations as tools and rejecting the nation as a supreme mystical entity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Higher-education financing is not discussed; Guénon criticises mass bookish education but proposes no remedy on debt.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The sources give no analysis of regional economic exploitation inside states; the school's concern is spiritual hierarchy and not core-periphery economics.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The school holds a single primordial truth beneath all orthodox traditions, which presupposes a common human spiritual constitution, though it opposes treating this as grounds for equal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; Guénon distrusts manufactured opinion in general.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Perennialist school's defining thesis is the transcendent unity of religions: one primordial tradition beneath the orthodox forms.

farm-price-support.rationale: The school regards economic questions as secondary; it admires agrarian traditional life but proposes no state farm policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Guénon and Evola do not address nuclear arms; adherents are split between quietism and warrior ethics.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: a hierarchy of natural functions rejects class-based and democratic party politics.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; adherents respect traditional customs but also traditional religious authority, so they are split.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchy of natural functions and the sex-differentiated roles of traditional societies, strongest in Evola.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Neither courts nor agencies are discussed; the school critiques modern materialism but offers no legal view.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: authority descends from a spiritual source and traditional elites, which supports a formal role for them.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The school rejects modern materialism and individualism but does not make environmental protection a priority; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Authority and order are favoured, but nothing is stated on judicial discretion versus fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on cultural and traditional order; not directly discussed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: No stated line; Guénon treats economic arrangements as secondary, and adherents split between organic corporate order and anti-statism.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; elections are rejected as a source of authority, so ID rules are beside the point.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: Perennialists see all orthodox religions as expressing one truth, but each tradition is to rule its own society in a hierarchy, not share parity within a state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Guénon rejects democracy as a product of the modern deviation, holding that authority comes from a spiritual source and not from the people.

premarital-sex.rationale: The school upholds traditional norms against modern permissiveness and individualism.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the preference for authority and order over liberal individual rights; not stated by the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from distrust of modern state welfare and equality; Guénon gives no economic programme.

women-suffrage.rationale: The school rejects equality as a modern dogma and favours a hierarchy of natural functions.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: It sees religion as the source of right order and blames modernity, not religion, for social decay.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Traditionalists reject modern scientism and Evola gives race a spiritual dimension, though Guénon says little.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The school rejects egalitarianism and holds sexes to have different natural functions, so state equality agencies would be opposed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's view that property and economy are secondary to spiritual order and that modern acquisitive individualism is a deviation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of egalitarian, universalist modern institutions; Evola explicitly despised such legalism.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Guénon reads scripture through its inner, symbolic meaning, so strictly literal inerrancy is not the school's line; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the school's belief in natural hierarchy and distinct male and female functions, against egalitarian guarantees.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Evola's hostility to communism and materialism, which he saw as the end of modern decline.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from authority descending from above through a hierarchy, not elected by the many.

national-church-status.rationale: Traditionalists hold all orthodox religions express one truth, but Evola was hostile to Christianity, so adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; Evola prized organic hierarchical empire over nation-states, and no stand on minority autonomy is documented.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from rejection of majority rule as a source of legitimacy.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by Guénon, who regarded politics as secondary, so no stated position.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the critique of modern materialism and consumption and the high value placed on ascetic discipline.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between valuing rooted peoples and the school's indifference to such policy.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Evola's warrior ideal and belief in distinct male and female roles, so equal conscription would be rejected.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from its stress on sacred, organic tradition rooted in place; Guenon did not address nations or land directly.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its hierarchical, authority-from-above order, which still presupposes legitimate rule and not summary killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from a school that treats foreign alignments as secondary to metaphysical principle.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from a school that sets social and national questions below spiritual ones; adherents split.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its rejection of equality as a pseudo-principle in favour of natural hierarchy.

self-ownership.rationale: It condemns modern individualism, so full individual self-ownership as a basic right runs against its view of persons within a hierarchy of functions.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from Guenon's view that economic arrangements are secondary.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from Guenon's view that economic arrangements are secondary.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its hierarchy of natural functions, which neither favours nor opposes party structures; Evola and Guenon differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its indifference to market policy; adherents split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: It holds that authority and society should be grounded in a shared orthodox spiritual tradition, so it does not treat politics as denomination-neutral.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: It sees modern civilization as a deviation from tradition and prefers return to the traditional order over a modern-plus-ancestral synthesis.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its defence of traditional social hierarchy and order; not stated by Guenon.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not a topic the ideology addresses; inferred from its lack of any economic doctrine.

distribution-by-process.rationale: No stated line; Guénon treats economic arrangements as downstream of metaphysical principle, and adherents are not agreed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Guénon criticises the dominance of economic factors but proposes no financial policy.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed by Guénon; Evola's racial writings and the school's rejection of equality mean adherents are split or silent on the question.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the view that authority descends from a spiritual source, so a rule cut off from that principle lacks true authority.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Guénon's criticism of industry and materialism as marks of the modern deviation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the school's defence of distinct traditional civilizations against a levelling modern world; Evola favours an organic empire over nationalism.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from Guénon's rejection of materialism and of economic factors as the basis of society.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchy of functions and the rejection of egalitarian, worker-centred politics; Evola sets empire above nationalism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of materialism; the school would not put wages and living standards first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of materialism and egalitarianism that underlie communist parties; the sources do not discuss the question.

missingStatements.text: All authentic religions express one underlying spiritual truth.
missingStatements.rationale: The Perennialist school's defining thesis is the transcendent unity of religions: one primordial tradition beneath the orthodox forms.

missingStatements.text: Society should be ordered into a hierarchy of functions, such as priests, warriors, merchants and labourers, each suited to a person's nature.
missingStatements.rationale: Guénon defines caste as individual nature fitted to function and blames its negation for the social chaos; Furlong reports Evola's hierarchical, differentiated order.

missingStatements.text: History is a long decline from a golden age and not a story of progress.
missingStatements.rationale: Guénon places the present in the Kali-Yuga, the last of four declining ages, and rejects progress as a lay dogma.

notes: The catalog entry resolves to a disambiguation page; this audit treats the Guénon-Schuon-Evola Perennialist school as the political sense not covered by other profiles. Guénon was politically quietist and called the social sphere secondary, so many political answers are inferred at low confidence; Evola's more activist and martial stance would raise some answers (war, military roles, strong state) and lower others (priestly rule). Mainstream Perennialists such as Schuon and Nasr are not political programmes and differ from Evola on race and war.
